thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty PDR-48291 fired — canary: model-serving (canary=10%) — p95 latency > 5s and 502 spike (10m window). Auto-suppression: false.

sre-taylor: acked on PD, I'm on it. grabbing logs and looking at canary cluster.

eng-jamal: thanks — just saw alerts. which commit rolled? deploy-bot: Deployed ref=feature/fast-tokenize @ 2026-03-15T02:15Z to cluster=canary-us-west.

eng-sam: copying metrics dashboard — saw CPU on the canary nodes jump ~3x, also a tokenization OOM in the logs.

ops-maria: any customer impact yet? metrics show an increase in 502s for hosted-api-east-1 but below 0.5% overall. likely impacting a subset of customers on edge region.

product-lina: flagged a paying customer who reported degraded response times. impact: degraded UX for streaming completions on a small percentage of requests.

sre-taylor: plan: 1) divert traffic off canary -> reduce canary to 0% 2) try immediate rollback of deploy if divert not stable 3) gather core logs and stack traces. starting with (1).

eng-jamal: I'm on the traffic control console. running command to set traffic weight to 0 for model-serving-canary:```curl -X POST "https://ops.redwood/traffic" -d '{"service":"model-serving","fraction":0,"target":"canary"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'```

eng-sam: saw this in the canary logs just before the spike:```ERROR: Tokenizer allocation failed: requested 1.6G, available 512M at tokenizer.c:214```

ops-maria: divert accepted, rolling traffic down to 0% (should take ~10s to propagate).

incident-bot: Traffic shift detected: canary fraction -> 0% (propagated to 8/8 routers).

sre-taylor: confirm p95 and 502 trends — jamal, can you post a p95 chart?

eng-jamal: p95 grafana link: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123/canary-latency — p95 dropped from 6.2s -> 1.1s after diversion. 502s returned to baseline.

product-lina: good, drop looks solid. what's root cause hypothesis?

eng-sam: initial data points: new tokenizer path uses different native allocator. likely regression in memory requests for some long-prompt paths. reproducing locally now with the failing seed.

sre-taylor: we should not roll this forward to prod. schedule rollback for the canary release and block rollout. jamal: can you trigger a rollback of deployment ref=feature/fast-tokenize on canary?

eng-jamal: issuing rollback:```kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-serving-canary --to-revision=42```

deploy-bot: Rollout undo started — revision=42 -> in_progress.

eng-sam: running a quick smoke test on the previous revision. Also collecting core dumps from the canary nodes:```scp canary-3:/var/crash/core.* /tmp/```

incident-bot: PD note: incident PDR-48291 acknowledged by sre-taylor, status=investigating. escalation on-call step preserved.

ops-maria: I've opened a support ticket template for the impacted customer: SUP-8892, will update once we have RCA.

sre-taylor: rollback completed and smoke tests green on canary for revision 42. Traffic remains at 0% then we will ramp to 10% with guardrails.

eng-jamal: verified previous revision p95 ~1.2s, no 502s. I'll incrementally ramp to 10% with short warmup windows:```for w in 1 2 5 10; do opsctl set-weight model-serving $w --wait 30; done```

sre-taylor: please keep an eye on GPU memory and tokenizer logs during ramp. if OOM or 5xx > 0.5% abort and revert to 0%.

eng-sam: note: we captured a core and stack trace pointing to native allocator path: tokenizer_native_alloc(). saving to infra bucket s3://redwood-incident/PDR-48291/ for the RL team.

product-lina: customer comms: sending an interim note. "We detected a performance regression in a canary release affecting a small subset of sessions. We diverted traffic and rolled back the canary; services have returned to normal for affected customers." Will send a follow-up with RCA timeline.

incident-bot: PD update: PDR-48291 -> status: mitigated (traffic diverted & rollback), assignee: sre-taylor. Next step: postmortem and follow-up tasks.

sre-taylor: quick action items assigned: - jamal: add e2e test for long prompts that triggered OOM - sam: PR to revert tokenizer allocator change and open an RFC for allocator sizing - maria: customer follow-up and support ticket updates - lina: draft postmortem and stakeholder comms.

eng-jamal: creating GH issue and linking failing test: https://github.com/redwood/infra/issues/4792

eng-sam: opened PR to revert change and added telemetry to detect memory regression. PR: https://github.com/redwood/model-serving/pull/2145

ops-maria: updated SUP-8892 with mitigation summary and ETA for RCA (48h).

product-lina: marking the incident as mitigated in the product tracker. we'll sync tomorrow at 10:00 PT for postmortem.

sre-taylor: closing PD incident for now but leaving thread open until postmortem is posted. great cross-team response, nice work. :clap:

eng-jamal: agree — quick detection and divert helped. logging notes in the incident bucket.

incident-bot: PDR-48291 closed by sre-taylor at 2026-03-15T02:22Z (mitigated).

sre-taylor: leaving final note — root cause: memory allocation regression from tokenizer native allocator in feature/fast-tokenize; mitigated via rollback and traffic diversion. follow-ups scheduled.

product-lina: thanks everyone.
